name: Sliding Window
description: Maintain a window (subarray/substring) defined by two pointers that expands and contracts based on a condition, avoiding recomputation of the window's stats from scratch each time.
core_technique: Expand the window by moving the right pointer; when the window violates a constraint, shrink from the left until it's valid again, updating a running aggregate (sum/count/set) incrementally rather than recomputing.
common_pitfalls: Recomputing window stats from scratch each iteration (defeats the purpose -- should be O(n) not O(n*k)); forgetting to shrink the window fully before comparing to the best answer; off-by-one on window size (k) vs window bounds (right - left + 1).

example_problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
example_problems.why_it_fits: Window grows while characters are unique, shrinks from the left when a duplicate is seen -- classic variable-size window with a hash set tracking window contents.

example_problems.title: Minimum Window Substring
example_problems.why_it_fits: Need the smallest window containing all target characters -- expand until valid, then aggressively shrink while it stays valid, tracking the minimum.

example_problems.title: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K
example_problems.why_it_fits: Fixed-size window -- simplest variant, just slide and maintain a running sum instead of recomputing.

additional_considerations: Distinguish fixed-size windows (simpler, just add new element and remove the one leaving) from variable-size windows (need a while-loop to shrink). For character-frequency windows, a hashmap/array of counts is usually cleaner than repeatedly scanning the window.
